national_news.title: PM Modi Inaugurates Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan in New Delhi
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the three-day Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission (founded in 1951 by Swami Chinmayananda).
Highlighted national efforts in cultural preservation, stating that India has successfully reclaimed over 650 stolen ancient idols and antiquities from abroad over the past 12 years.
Emphasized key aspects of the National Education Policy (NEP), including education in the mother tongue, integration of traditional knowledge, and focus on modern science and emerging technologies.

national_news.title: India and China Agree to Utilize Diplomatic and Military Channels for LAC Management
bullets: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) stated that India and China agreed to discuss measures to improve understanding of the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and prevent border miscalculations.
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed that India continues to transport life-saving medicines to Iran as a humanitarian gesture despite regional flight connectivity challenges.
The ministry confirmed the safety of 14 Indian nationals in Hodeidah, Yemen, and facilitated the return of over 13,000 Umrah pilgrims stranded in Saudi Arabia.

national_news.title: President Murmu Addresses Bastar Dussehra Festival and Muria Darbar in Chhattisgarh
bullets: President Droupadi Murmu highlighted combined central and state efforts in overcoming Naxalism during her visit to the Bastar Dussehra Festival in Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh.
The President attended the traditional 'Muria Darbar' at Sirhasar Bhavan, emphasizing its role as a democratic platform for tribal communities to air grievances to leaders.
Emphasized equitable development for tribal entrepreneurs and youth to contribute towards the national goal of 'Viksit Bharat @2047'.

national_news.title: India Achieves Milestones at Asian Para Games with Multiple Medals and World Record
bullets: Sandeep Kumar secured the Gold medal in the Men's 400m T64 event with a new World Record, which marked India's 100th medal at the Asian Para Games.
Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan won India's first-ever medal in the Women's Recurve Doubles event at the Games.
Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi clinched Gold in Men's Recurve Doubles, while Nitesh Kumar and Naveen Sivakumar earned Gold in Badminton Men's Singles.

national_news.title: India Counters Pakistan's Allegations on Religious Freedom at United Nations
bullets: First Secretary at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, rejected Pakistan's statements during a discussion on the UN Special Rapporteur's interim report.
India highlighted the respectful burial of Pakistani soldiers by the Indian Army with military honours during the 1999 Kargil War, despite Pakistan's initial refusal to claim them.
Criticized Pakistan's minority rights record and urged UN reports to give due weight to the human rights of terrorism victims rather than selectively highlighting concerns.

national_news.title: Satellite-Tagged Amur Falcons Complete Migration Journey to Manipur
bullets: Two satellite-tagged Amur Falcons, named 'Apapang' and 'Alang', returned to Manipur after migrating across 23 countries in Asia and Africa.
The birds were tagged by scientists from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) and traveled from their breeding grounds in northeastern China in 11 days.
After stopovers in the Tamenglong district of Manipur, the falcons will undertake a non-stop 6,000 km flight to Somalia, including a 3,000 km Arabian Sea crossing.

national_news.title: CAQM Reviews Paddy Stubble Management Measures in Punjab
bullets: A high-level team from the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) conducted field reviews in Ropar, Hoshiarpur, and Amritsar districts of Punjab.
The review assessed in-situ and ex-situ Crop Residue Management (CRM) measures, including biomass plants, Krishi Vigyan Kendra machinery availability, and Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) plants.
CAQM directed state authorities to enforce compulsory co-firing targets of paddy stubble in thermal power plants to curb stubble burning incidents in NCR and adjoining areas.

national_news.title: Defence Minister Addresses Army Commanders' Conference; Releases Land Warfare Doctrine
bullets: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh addressed the Army Commanders' Conference, emphasizing a 20-30 year long-term strategic vision and releasing the Land Warfare Doctrine.
Defence production in India reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, with defence exports achieving an all-time high of approximately Rs 38,000 crore.
Highlighted the success of Operation Sindoor and urged the military to accelerate integration of Artificial Intelligence, autonomous systems, cybersecurity, and modern drone technology.

national_news.title: India's Data Centre Capacity Projected to Reach 8,000 MW by CY30
bullets: India's data centre capacity increased from 375 MW in CY20 to 1,575 MW in 2026, with projections to expand to 8,000 MW by CY30.
Ministry of Power estimates data centre electricity demand will reach 17 GW by 2031-32, with sector investments scaling from Rs 0.36 trillion in FY26 to Rs 1.31 trillion by FY32.
To manage high resource consumption—where a 100MW facility requires up to 2.5 billion litres of water annually—innovative technologies like deep seawater cooling are being explored.

national_news.title: C-DAC and Bank of India Partner to Develop Quantum Technologies for Banking
bullets: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) signed an MoU with Bank of India to co-develop indigenous quantum technologies for the financial sector.
The partnership aims to build a Quantum Ecosystem for Financial Innovation, focusing on quantum-safe technologies, operational resilience, and advanced cybersecurity.
Scope of collaboration extends to AI-driven fraud detection, credit analytics, smart contracts, blockchain applications, and technical capacity-building.

national_news.title: DDWS Organises Virtual Conference on Convergence of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and 16th Finance Commission
bullets: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, conducted a national virtual conference emphasizing convergence between Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and 16th Finance Commission grants.

With JJM 2.0, the core focus has shifted from initial infrastructure creation to long-term functionality, source sustainability, and robust Operation & Maintenance (O&M) of rural drinking water systems.

Gram Panchayats are tasked under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment to lead annual O&M planning, utilizing tied Rural Local Body (RLB) grants for maintaining service delivery and source sustainability.

national_news.title: India and China Discuss LAC Understanding and Border Management
bullets: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) stated that India and China continue to use diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve border issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
Both sides agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas to ensure better border management and avoid miscalculations.
India reaffirmed its commitment to facilitating the transport of life-saving medicines to Iran as a humanitarian gesture amidst regional challenges.

national_news.title: India Exercises Right of Reply Against Pakistan at the United Nations
bullets: India criticized Pakistan at the UN over remarks on religious freedom and burial rights during discussions on an interim report by the UN Special Rapporteur.
First Secretary Bhavika Mangalanandan recalled Pakistan's historical refusal to acknowledge the bodies of its soldiers killed in the 1999 Kargil War.
India highlighted that the Indian Army had buried Pakistani soldiers with military honors according to Islamic rites, while criticizing Pakistan's treatment of minorities.

national_news.title: India and Uzbekistan Hold 10th Joint Working Group Meeting on Counter Terrorism
bullets: The 10th meeting of the India-Uzbekistan Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism was held in New Delhi.
Discussions focused on countering extremism, radicalization, terror financing, misuse of technology, and transnational organized crime.
Both nations reaffirmed their commitment to cooperate in multilateral forums including the UN, SCO-RATS, and EAG.

bihar_news.title: CtrlS to Invest ₹10,000 Crore for AI Factory in Bodh Gaya and Open Patna Data Centre
bullets: CtrlS Datacenters signed a letter of intent with the Bihar government to invest ₹10,000 crore in a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya.
The company inaugurated a ₹400 crore data centre with an initial IT load capacity of 12 MW in the Patliputra Industrial Area, Patna.
The Patna facility is designed to serve enterprises, government institutions, and technology businesses across Bihar and eastern India.

bihar_news.title: ICAR-MGIFRI Motihari Participates in National Launch of Khet Bachao Abhiyan - Rabi 2026
bullets: ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute (MGIFRI), Motihari, participated in the national launch of Khet Bachao Abhiyan (KBA) – Rabi 2026.
Six multidisciplinary scientific teams were formed to conduct village-level awareness programmes, farmer-scientist interactions, and field demonstrations from October 22 to November 30, 2026.
The campaign focuses on balanced fertilizer use, soil health management, natural farming, crop diversification, and prevention of crop residue burning.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government Plans to Develop Jamui's Kukurjhap Dam as Eco-Tourism Hub
bullets: The Bihar government plans to develop Kukurjhap Dam located in Barhat block, Jamui district, as an eco-tourism hub with adventure facilities under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.
The project is being overseen by the Bihar State Eco-Tourism Development Society as part of the Unified Eco-Tourism Master Plan.
The master plan covers 7 ecologically rich districts/areas including Paschim Champaran, Rohtas, Kaimur, Jamui, Banka, Nawada, and Valmiki Nagar.

bihar_news.title: Biennial Elections Held for Eight Bihar Legislative Council Seats
bullets: Polling conducted for eight Bihar Legislative Council (MLC) seats across Graduates' and Teachers' constituencies, covering 5.32 lakh eligible voters and 150 candidates.
Saran Teachers' constituency recorded the highest turnout at 13.56% in the initial hours, while Darbhanga led among Graduates' constituencies.
The elections feature 933 polling stations with votes scheduled for counting on October 27, witnessing key political contests including the Patna Graduates seat.
